scopeNote: No separate recovered Magi line-map is asserted. These are two explicitly separated Zoroastrian textual comparison layers.

traditions.label: Zoroastrian (Avestan names)
traditions.description: Three securely identified stellar names shown with unconnected reference markers; Vanant and Satavaēsa remain unplotted candidates.
traditions.period: Younger Avestan textual tradition; date of composition not fixed by this layer.
traditions.geometryNotice: Rings mark modern reference stars for identified objects. No surviving Avestan stick figures or complete Magi sky map are asserted.

source.authors: Mazzaroth project; Avestan text after Geldner; astronomical identifications discussed by D. N. MacKenzie and Antonio Panaino

source.changes: Selected three supported object identifications. Modern catalogue members serve only as unconnected locators; no connecting lines or hypothetical outlines were reconstructed.

constellations.name: Tištrya · Sirius
constellations.evidence: Named in Yašt 8; Panaino identifies the star with Sirius.
constellations.notes: The ring locates Sirius itself. This is a stellar identification, not a constellation outline.

constellations.name: Haptōiringa · Great Bear
constellations.evidence: Yašt 8.12 names Haptōiringa; Iranian studies identify it with the Great Bear.
constellations.notes: Seven Big Dipper stars are modern reference members for the attested seven-star group. They are deliberately not joined into an asserted Avestan drawing.

constellations.name: Paoiryaēinyas · Pleiades
constellations.evidence: Yašt 8.12 preserves the name; MacKenzie identifies the group as the Pleiades.
constellations.notes: The atlas’s nine catalogue reference members locate the cluster. This display choice does not assert an ancient Iranian count of nine stars.

sources.label: D. N. MacKenzie, Constellations, Encyclopaedia Iranica (1992)

unlocated.name: Vanant
unlocated.evidence: Named in Yašt 8.12; Vega is used in modern Iranian studies.
unlocated.notes: Retained as an unplotted candidate while historical identifications and their periods are reviewed. It is not silently substituted for a later Bundahishn stellar chief.

sources.label: Encyclopaedia Iranica, Mithra i., discussion of Vanant (Yašt 21.1)

unlocated.name: Satavaēsa
unlocated.evidence: Yašt 8.0 and 8.9 name the astral collaborator of Tištrya; Panaino calls the Fomalhaut identification probable.
unlocated.notes: The candidate is retained without fixed plotted coordinates. Later stellar-chief lists and translations must not be assumed to settle the identification.

sources.label: D. N. MacKenzie, Constellations, Encyclopaedia Iranica (1992)
M. A. Dandamayev, Magi, Encyclopaedia Iranica

traditions.label: Zoroastrian (Bundahishn zodiac)
traditions.description: Twelve Middle Persian zodiac names from the Bundahishn, shown on explicitly modern comparison figures.
traditions.period: Middle Persian Bundahishn tradition, preserved in medieval recensions; not a dated Achaemenid or Magi map.
traditions.geometryNotice: The text supplies zodiac names, not these star-to-star lines. Modern Western figures locate the names; they are not 30° zodiac sectors or recovered Pahlavi outlines.

source.authors: Mazzaroth project; names after E. W. West’s Bundahishn translation; modern reference figures by Stellarium’s team
